report_name: Microsoft Defender Halts Ransomware Abusing 'mshta.exe' in 128 Seconds

attack_patterns.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Mshta
attack_patterns.description: The legitimate Windows binary 'mshta.exe' was used to download and execute a remote malicious payload from attacker infrastructure as a living-off-the-land technique.

attack_patterns.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
attack_patterns.description: The attacker's script, executed via mshta.exe, attempted to establish persistence by manipulating RunMRU registry keys.

tools.name: Mshta
tools.description: Legitimate Windows binary used to download and execute a remote malicious payload as part of a living-off-the-land technique.

identities.name: QNET
identities.description: The company targeted by the ransomware attack, which was successfully disrupted by Microsoft Defender.

infrastructure.name: Attacker Payload Delivery Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Remote infrastructure used to host and deliver a malicious payload executed by mshta.exe.

indicators.name: Suspicious Mshta.exe Network Connection
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Mshta.exe Network Connection
id: 2b8a1c3d-f4e5-4b9a-8c7d-6e5f4a3b2c1d
status: experimental
description: Detects mshta.exe executing a remote HTA file, a common living-off-the-land technique used to download and run malicious scripts.
references:
  - https://gbhackers.com/ransomware-abuses-windows-tool/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-05
tags:
  - attack.t1218.005
  - attack.defense_evasion
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\mshta.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of mshta.exe with a command line containing a URL, indicating it is fetching a remote payload. This was the initial vector in the QNET attack.

indicators.name: Potential Persistence via RunMRU Key Modification
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Potential Persistence via RunMRU Key Modification
id: 9e8d7c6b-5a4b-4c3d-b2a1-f0e9d8c7b6a5
status: experimental
description: Detects modification of the RunMRU registry key, which was observed in a ransomware pre-attack sequence. While this key tracks recently used commands, modification can indicate an attempt to establish persistence or hide execution artifacts.
references:
  - https://gbhackers.com/ransomware-abuses-windows-tool/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-05
tags:
  - attack.t1547.001
  - attack.persistence
level: medium
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetObject|endswith: '\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\RunMRU'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects modification of the RunMRU registry key, which was observed being used for persistence in the described ransomware attack.
